results.title: Effectiveness of workplace health promotion programs for industrial workers: a systematic review | BMC Public Health | Springer Nature Link
results.content: # Effectiveness of workplace health promotion programs for industrial workers: a systematic review. Workplace health promotion is essential for individual and organisational well-being and disease prevention, also in industrial workers. As the transfer of the evidence on the effectiveness of such programs into practice is limited due to scattered effects, the need for a consolidation of the available studies is given. The purpose of this systematic review was to synthesise the evidence on the effectiveness of workplace health promotion programs for industrial workers. Outcomes were workplace health interventions’ safety and corresponding health-related outcomes. Generally, the mean quality of the studies was moderate, with most studies judged with a high overall risk of bias. The studies included in this review provide evidence that workplace health promotion can be effective. ### Effectiveness of work-related interventions for return to work in people on sick leave: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
